newsitem.title: USA: U.S. illegal immigration population increases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. illegal immigration population increases.

text.p: The number of illegal immigrants in the United States increased to five million in October 1996 from an estimated 3.9 million in 1992, the U.S. Justice Department reported on Friday.
The department's Immigration and Naturalisation Service said nearly 60 percent of the total illegal population had entered the country illegally, while the rest had overstayed their visas.
The illegal immigrants accounted for about 2 percent of the total U.S. population, it said.
More than half of the illegal resident population came from Mexico, followed by El Salvador, Guatemala, Canada and Haiti, immigration officials said.
They said the estimated population from Mexico rose by more than 150,000 annually through the last eight years.

The officials said more than 80 percent of the illegal residents settled in California, Texas, New York, Florida, Illinois, New Jersey and Arizona, the states traditionally with the largest immigrant populations.
An estimated two million illegal immigrants lived in California in October 1996, followed by Texas at 700,000.
INS officials, who have been trying to curb the flow of illegal aliens into the country, said the average annual growth rate in the population has been revised downward to 275,000 from 300,000.
The estimates cover those individuals who have established residence in the United States by remaining here illegally for more than a year.
